_doc: The fleet gate (speakerguardd-gate): policy only, no hardware. speakerguardd v2 runs on a board only if the protection unit its own tuning names is in units_at_parity and, while require_qualified_board is true, the board is in that unit's qualified list (a passing audible run on the shipped tree). Fleet cutover: spp3, lsm2 and atsp are in units_at_parity and require_qualified_board is true, so v2 runs only on the boards in their unit's qualified list. Those boards were audited and qualified on silent hardware runs (spp3), on silent and audible runs (lsm2) or derive cleanly and pass the synthetic end-to-end tests (atsp). Other spp3 boards whose graphs compile (other MacBook Pro and Air speaker sets) stay on the older daemons until each has had the per-band rig against macOS's own graph; then it joins its unit's list. Setting require_qualified_board to false lets every board whose tuning names a parity unit run v2 (day one for new Macs), and waits for that rig coverage. The kernel decides the rest: v2 runs only on a kernel with the Speaker Protection interface, the older daemons only on one without it. Every distribution ships this file unchanged. The atsp list holds the boards whose device tree and tuning derive cleanly (wiring.py) and that pass the synthetic end-to-end tests; none of them has had an audible run. The j473 (Mac mini M2) is also qualified on its own tuning: its collected bundle derives with no hand values to the fixture's wiring, every rig case on its own one-channel preset (law families, host slices, bypass, masks, AudioUnitReset, music) is bit-identical to macOS within full scale, and its live macOS speaker path runs that preset at 48 kHz. atsp joined units_at_parity on 2026-11-05: on the 25G83 differential rig all 117 atsp cases (every law family, every shipped profile, one- and multi-channel, every host call size, bypass and masks) are bit-identical to macOS (SPEC-ATSP 11). lsm2 left units_at_parity on 2026-11-05, when the 25G83 differential rig showed its velocity band gains up to 3.8 dB louder than macOS on low-frequency tones (fb2-fb9, w1 law cases). It rejoined on 2026-11-07: on the arm64 differential rig all 340 lsm2 cases hold every Apple limit (velocity, displacement, temperature, power) with at least the margin macOS keeps, and the ceiling family follows the macOS coil trajectory exactly. Loudness itself is not the criterion. The j700 is lsm2's only qualified board: it qualifies on its own tuning with a silent and an audible run on the shipped tree. Other lsm2 boards (j713, j813) stay on the older daemons until each has its own run.
_voicing_pre_doc: Full generated voicing per physical board: literal true enables it. Empty/default false keeps the interim convolver. SPP3V owns promotion after numerical/acoustic qualification. Provision again after any change.
_voicing_pre_bound_doc: Interim never-louder bound (Ryan 2026-11-07: Plan A tonight on all four boards, open laws in their never-louder form): one gain in dB per unit lane, applied by the PipeWire voicing graph after the voicing plugin, so no lane of the generated voicing is louder than macOS while the Comp onset/param-69 (all four), AID44 q2 detector laws are still open (j413 woofers: -1.09 dB since the exact LowFlow landed, 2026-11-08, covering the Comp onset excess the exact LowFlow now passes through). Derived from the full-chain safety scan (packaging: bound.py = worst louder excess + 0.03 dB, L/R pairs equal) for j316s/j413/j616s and from the AID44 voicing-level VLS gate for j700; protection is unchanged and governs. Each entry goes when its board's laws are exact.
_voicing_pre_lowpass_doc: INTERIM never-louder band limit, not a macOS law (AUD-CUT2 2026-11-07, Ryan's parity rule: never-louder is fine as interim). {hz, order}: an even-order Butterworth low-pass built from PipeWire bq_lowpass sections in FRONT of the voicing plugin. j700 only: v2's AID44 ControlFreak lacks the AU's reconstruction low-pass, so above ~17 kHz the box is up to +23 dB (+30 dB at 0 dBFS) louder than macOS and its saturation aliases a loud high-frequency input into 9-16.5 kHz; the lane trim cannot hold either. 17.4 kHz order 8 (with the j700 trim): AID44 box rig (installed AU, 362 tones/pink/steps incl. 16-23.75 kHz probes) 0 louder cases, worst -0.58 dB; full AID44 voicing VLS 30 Hz-19.5 kHz 0 louder bands, worst -0.03 dB; cost at 16 kHz -0.1 dB. Goes when the ControlFreak law is exact (Daybreak t-5511). 2026-11-08: no board carries it; the AID44 ControlFreak saturation, reconstruction and drive laws are exact on the box rig (steady and 20 kHz), so the j700 trim alone (-0.35 dB from the AID44 VLS, worst +0.311) holds.
